steps.name: Load, normalize and characterize the treated/control pair
caveats: Salmon gene-level counts may carry length correction; the profile does not say. Do not apply a second length normalization.
Very low-count genes dominate extreme fold changes; do not interpret them without the mean-expression axis.
A high correlation between the two samples does not prove absence of treatment effect and a low one does not prove presence — with n=1 the two are confounded with technical variation.
steps.context: Design is 1 treated vs 1 control liver sample, raw gene-level counts from salmon, human (taxon 9606), no biological replication. The MA plot and log2FC spread are the only available read on how noisy this comparison is: a wide spread among low-count genes is technical, not biological.
steps.question: After library-size normalization, how similar are the single treated and single control liver samples in counts.csv, and how much of the 12,000-gene matrix shows a large apparent change?
constraints: Use the actual sample identifiers and condition labels read from metadata.csv; do not hard-code names.
Do NOT run DESeq2 or edgeR dispersion estimation in this step and do NOT emit any p-value or FDR here.
Report library sizes and detection counts for both samples explicitly in the output.
If counts are non-integer (salmon estimated counts), state this and round only for downstream count-based tools, keeping the un-rounded values for CPM.
State in the output text that with n=1 per group no statistical test of differential expression is possible.
steps.description: Read /eval-four-models-v2-without-no-replicates-1v1-s1-1/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (12,000 genes x 2 sample columns) and /eval-four-models-v2-without-no-replicates-1v1-s1-1/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv (2 rows: sample id + condition). Confirm the metadata sample identifiers match the count-matrix column names exactly and that the two conditions are one treated and one control; report the literal condition labels found rather than assuming names. Verify counts are non-negative integers (they came from salmon, so they may be non-integer estimated counts — if so, round for count-based tools and say so). Report per-sample library size, number of genes with zero counts in each sample, and detection counts. Compute CPM and log2-CPM with a prior count, filter to genes with sufficient evidence (e.g. CPM >= 1 in at least one sample), and characterize the pair: Spearman and Pearson correlation on log-CPM, an MA plot (mean log-expression vs log2 fold change), the distribution of log2FC, and the fraction of retained genes with |log2FC| > 1 and > 2. Save the filtered normalized matrix and the per-gene log2FC table for the next step.
acceptance_criteria: Sample IDs in metadata.csv are confirmed to match count-matrix columns, and both condition labels are reported verbatim.
Per-sample library size, detected-gene count and zero-count gene count are reported for both samples.
A filtered, library-size-normalized log-CPM matrix and a per-gene log2FC table are written to disk.
An MA plot and a log2FC distribution plot are produced.
Pearson and Spearman correlation between the two samples on log-CPM are reported, along with the fraction of genes exceeding |log2FC| of 1 and 2.
Output explicitly states that no p-values are computed because there is no within-condition replication.

steps.name: Ranked candidate gene list with fixed-dispersion sensitivity check
caveats: With BCV = 0.1 the exactTest will call a large number of genes 'significant'; this reflects the assumption, not the data, and must not be reported as a finding.
Genes with zero counts in one sample give infinite raw fold changes — handle with a prior count and flag them.
Do not use apeglm/ashr shrinkage results as if they conferred statistical support; shrinkage without replicates only reshapes the ranking.
steps.context: This is the answer step for 'which genes are differentially expressed'. The scientifically honest answer is that differential expression cannot be established from 1 vs 1; what can be delivered is a fold-change ranking plus an explicit demonstration of how dependent any apparent significance is on the dispersion one assumes. edgeR 4.10.3 and DESeq2 1.52.0 are both installed; edgeR's exactTest accepts a supplied dispersion and is the standard route for the no-replicate case as documented in the edgeR user guide.
steps.question: Which genes show the largest treated-vs-control fold change in this single-pair liver comparison, and how does that ranking shift under plausible assumed biological variability?
constraints: Do NOT let edgeR or DESeq2 estimate dispersion from the data — supply the dispersion explicitly at each of the three BCV values.
Report the three assumed-BCV significance counts side by side; never present one of them as the result.
Column names carrying p-values or FDR must encode the assumed BCV in the name.
Every written table and figure must carry the n=1 caveat in a header comment or caption.
Use the same filtered gene set as T1S1 so gene counts are consistent across steps.
Rank primarily by fold change with low-count damping; do not sort the headline list by an assumed-dispersion p-value.
steps.description: Produce the deliverable the research question asks for, framed correctly as a CANDIDATE list, not a tested DE result. Starting from the filtered normalized matrix and log2FC table from T1S1: (a) rank genes by log2FC computed on CPM with a prior count that damps low-count instability, and separately by a count-weighted statistic that downweights genes with low total counts, and report the top 50 up and top 50 down under each ranking plus their overlap; (b) as a sensitivity analysis, run edgeR's exactTest with a FIXED, user-supplied dispersion at three assumed BCV values (0.1 for a technical/cell-line-like replicate, 0.2 as edgeR's common recommendation for well-controlled human experiments, 0.4 for typical human tissue variability) and report how the number of genes passing FDR < 0.05 changes across the three — the point of this is to show the result is an artefact of the assumed dispersion, not evidence. Emit one merged results table: gene, mean expression, log2FC, and the three assumed-BCV p-value/FDR columns each named to make the assumption explicit (e.g. pvalue_assumedBCV0.2). Every output file and figure must carry a header line stating that n=1 per condition, that the p-values derive from an assumed rather than estimated dispersion, and that the ranking is hypothesis-generating and requires replicated follow-up.
acceptance_criteria: A merged per-gene table is written containing mean expression, log2FC, and p-value/FDR columns for each of BCV = 0.1, 0.2 and 0.4, with the assumption in each column name.
Top 50 up- and down-changed genes are reported under both the fold-change and count-weighted rankings, with the overlap between rankings quantified.
The count of genes at FDR < 0.05 is reported separately for all three assumed BCV values and the sensitivity of that count to the assumption is stated in words.
A volcano-style or ranked-fold-change figure is produced, captioned with the no-replication caveat.
Output states plainly that these are candidates from an unreplicated comparison, not established differentially expressed genes.

steps.name: Gene-set level read-out of the fold-change ranking
caveats: GO-BP sets are heavily nested; collapse redundant parent/child hits before reporting a count of significant processes.
Enrichment FDR here controls multiplicity across gene sets only — it does nothing about the absence of biological replication.
Liver bulk RNA-seq is dominated by a small number of very highly expressed hepatic genes; check that top enrichment hits are not driven entirely by those.
steps.context: Aggregating many genes into a set partially averages out single-sample technical noise, so the gene-set view is the more defensible layer of interpretation for a 1v1 design — but only as direction-of-change evidence. Human hallmark (50 sets) and human GO-BP (7,538 sets) GMTs with HGNC symbols were visible in the reference store at planning time, as was a human UniProt ID-mapping table for identifier conversion. gseapy 1.3.1 and decoupler 2.2.0 are installed.
steps.question: Do the treated-vs-control fold changes in this liver pair aggregate into any coherent hallmark or GO biological-process signal, which would be more robust to single-sample noise than any individual gene call?
constraints: Use HUMAN gene sets only — the dataset is Homo sapiens liver; do not fall back to the mouse or rat collections.
Rank the full filtered gene list by log2FC for the preranked run; do not pre-filter by any assumed-dispersion p-value.
Report the identifier mapping rate from count-matrix row IDs to gene symbols before running enrichment.
Caption all enrichment outputs with the n=1-per-condition caveat.
If a required gene-set collection is not present at run time, say which and continue with what is available rather than substituting a different organism or collection.
steps.description: Run a preranked gene-set enrichment on the full log2FC ranking from T1S2 (all filtered genes, ranked by log2FC), plus an overrepresentation test on the top/bottom fold-change tails, against human hallmark gene sets and human GO biological-process gene sets. The reference data needed is: a hallmark gene-set collection for human with HGNC gene symbols, and a GO biological-process gene-set collection for human with HGNC gene symbols — both are present in the environment's staged pathway references; resolve them at run time rather than assuming a path, and confirm the organism is human before use. First check the identifier space of the count matrix row names: if they are Ensembl gene IDs or Entrez IDs rather than HGNC symbols, map them to symbols using the staged human ID-mapping resource and report the mapping rate; if fewer than 60% map, report that and stop rather than enriching a badly mapped list. Report normalized enrichment scores, nominal p, and FDR, and note that the preranked p-values inherit no replication-based error control — the ranking they operate on comes from a single pair, so a leading-edge set is a hypothesis about direction, not a tested pathway change. If either gene-set collection is absent at run time, report which one was missing and proceed with whichever is available; if neither is available, report that and skip the step without failing the run.
acceptance_criteria: Identifier space of the count matrix is reported, with the symbol-mapping rate if conversion was required.
Preranked enrichment results against human hallmark sets are written with NES, nominal p and FDR.
Overrepresentation results for the top and bottom fold-change tails against human GO biological process are written, with the tail size used stated explicitly.
Leading-edge genes are reported for the top-ranked sets.
Output states that enrichment inherits the unreplicated design and is directional evidence only.
If a gene-set resource was missing, the output names it and the step still completes.

plan.title: 1v1 liver treated vs control: descriptive fold-change ranking
plan.analytical_narrative: The input is a 12,000-gene x 2-sample salmon count matrix (counts.csv) with a 2-row metadata table giving one treated and one control liver sample. With n=1 per condition there is no within-condition variance, so no test statistic, no p-value and no FDR can be estimated from these data — any DESeq2/edgeR run would either refuse to fit dispersion or fabricate it from an assumed value. The plan is therefore honest about what is obtainable: (T1S1) load, sanity-check and library-size-normalize the two samples, quantify the global similarity of the pair (MA plot, correlation, fraction of genes with |log2FC| > 1) so the reader can judge whether the treatment effect is large relative to technical noise; (T1S2) produce a ranked descriptive fold-change table with shrinkage-free and count-weighted rankings, explicitly labelled as a candidate list rather than a differential-expression result, plus a fixed-dispersion edgeR exactTest sensitivity check whose p-values are reported only as a rank heuristic with the assumed BCV stated; (T1S3) an optional, clearly-caveated GSEA-preranked / hallmark and GO-BP overrepresentation pass on the fold-change ranking, since gene-set aggregation is more robust to single-sample noise than any individual gene call, using the human hallmark and GO-BP GMTs staged under /mnt/refs. The design caveat — no biological replication — is carried into every step's output so the synthesizer cannot present these as tested DE genes.
